Senses.Explanation: The finest speck of dust is the smallest possible remainder or obstruction. Hengshan Weili asks how even a speck could stand when no position facing the Buddha remains. Yuanwu Keqin says both that no speck is established and that two facing mirrors have no speck between them. An unnamed monk asks Luohan Zhiyi why beautiful and ugly still appear if no speck is established. Dahui Zonggao says the great round mirror contains no speck and therefore admits no stray furniture. Panshan Baoji asks what speck could stand when the mind has no business and things do not arise. The dust image is thus repeatedly used to press whether the slightest remainder has been left standing.

Senses.Explanation: Shoushan's bamboo staff names the public case in which Shoushan Xingnian raises a bamboo staff and says: 'If you call it a bamboo staff, you run into it; if you do not call it a bamboo staff, you turn away from it. What do you call it?' Wumen Huikai transmits the exchange, repeats the two prohibitions, forbids both speech and silence, and demands an immediate answer. Two biographies recount the layman Huang Yanjie raising the case as far as Yexian, seizing the staff, breaking it, throwing it down, and asking what it is; the answer is 'Blind!' Yongji Rong's verse says the staff leads blind people into two and three while a sharp monk snatches it and presents it face-to-face. Xiangya Ting's verse places its flower inside an iron tree and says that deliberation leaves one a thousand miles away. The later handling and verses remain attached to Shoushan's original call-it/do-not-call-it test.
